# fix(authz+sync): a receipt collision was destroying audit records, and the merge that never merged

<!-- Generated by SessionEnd hook from a commit matching a journal-worthy pattern.
     Next session: review, then promote to a real journal entry OR delete. -->

**Commit**: `f154548b6e52` — fix(authz+sync): a receipt collision was destroying audit records, and the merge that never merged

**Body**:

Two filed defects, both tested against the tree before implementing. One of them was
reported with the wrong mechanism AGAIN -- the fourth today -- and this time the
mechanism was more severe than filed, not less.

#88 DEFECT 2 -- THERE WAS NO REFUSAL TO PRESERVE.

The report said a colliding same-day receipt was "refused" and proposed only to
disambiguate the filename, "preserving the refusal-to-overwrite invariant". Measured:
`writeFileSync` carried no `wx` flag. There was no such invariant. The second write
SILENTLY DESTROYED the first receipt, including its verbatim authorizing instruction.

Since a receipt is the ONLY distinguisher between an authorized cross-repo action and
an unauthorized one (repo-scope-discipline.md condition 4 -- "present = in-scope,
absent = critical L1"), that is audit-record destruction, not an ergonomics annoyance.
Proven worse still: a cheap `--mode read` receipt for the same action DESTROYED an
existing `write` authorization, after which the hook reported the authorized write as
unauthorized -- defeating by filename collision the very read/write tier the tool's own
comments call "the design's central tier".

So both halves were required, not just the filename one: the `wx` refusal (the
invariant that was assumed to exist) AND a digest over the full untruncated
(target, action, mode) triple, taken where the 48-char slug stops discriminating.

#64 -- THE HEADLINE PROMISED MERGE, THE RULE PERFORMED REPLACE.

Reconciled toward the truth rather than the promise: the command now says
"category-based replace, NOT a per-file merge" and states plainly that a local edit to
a shared artifact is discarded with no conflict and no warning. Adds the missing
sanctioned local namespace (`rules/project/`, `commands/project/`) and preserves
`team-memory/**` (per-repo signed state, same class as `learning/**`).

The acceptance criterion that mattered most -- report what a sync would discard -- is
now MECHANICAL, not a prose promise: `sync-preflight-local-mods.mjs` splits
DIFFERS-and-stale from DIFFERS-and-consumer-authored and exits 2 only for the latter.
Without that split every differing file alarms on a healthy consumer and the gate gets
ignored.

TESTED, AND THE TESTS WERE SHOWN TO DISCRIMINATE.

35 checks across two committed fixture runners. The #88 suite run against the pre-fix
tool: PASS 9 / FAIL 8, so its greens are evidence rather than decoration. The #64 tool
is new, so each predicate was mutation-tested instead -- six mutations, each confirmed
APPLIED and each redding ONLY its own predicate.

Two things the real-data walk caught that fixtures alone would not have. The default
sync-subject pattern was a plausible guess that misclassified 59 of 82 real artifacts
as consumer-authored; re-derived from observed history it went 59 -> 34 -> 10, and the
residual 10 are genuine local edits. And a `--json | head` reading gave me head's exit
status, not the tool's -- the truncation trap, caught by re-measuring without the pipe.

T9 is the anti-recurrence lock: #64 IS one contract stated in two places that drifted,
so the parity test parses the command's Preserved list and asserts set equality with
the tool's constant. Mutating either side reds it.

Pre-existing suite state recorded rather than implied: 10 audit-fixture runners fail on
a clean tree at this commit, and the identical 10 fail with these changes -- verified by
stashing. No regression is claimed beyond that measurement.

Durability: bin/**, commands/** and audit-fixtures/** are all synced globs, so this is a
Class-A stopgap for consumers pulling today. The durable surface is the proposal.

sync-from-template.md is 188 lines against the 150 cap -- a pre-existing 174 plus 14
load-bearing contract lines; named rationale per cc-artifacts.md Rule 3 (ordered
procedural runbook, redundancy trimmed first).
